scope: Threads and Synchronisation (the current corpus scope)

objectives.objective: Explain what a thread is, what threads of one process share and what each thread has privately (stack, registers, program counter).
Use pthread_create and pthread_join correctly, including passing arguments to and returning results from a thread.
Identify a race condition on shared data, explain why a non-atomic update such as counter++ loses updates, and define a critical section.
Explain how a lock enforces mutual exclusion, how hardware primitives (test-and-set, compare-and-swap) build one, and when to spin versus sleep.
Describe sem_wait and sem_post, and use a semaphore as a lock (initial value 1) and for ordering (initial value 0).
Use a condition variable with its mutex, and explain why waiting must re-check the condition in a while loop.
Explain and solve producer-consumer, readers-writers and dining philosophers, including the ordering pitfalls of each.
Recognise deadlock (its four conditions), atomicity-violation and order-violation bugs, and apply a prevention technique such as lock ordering.
